description: The provided image is a donut chart illustrating the hierarchical structure of the MMAR benchmark, which is designed for deep reasoning in speech, audio, and music. The chart is divided into three main concentric layers: the innermost layer represents the "Perception" layer, the middle layer is the "Semantic Layer (41.2%)", and the outermost layer is the "Content Analysis" layer. The "Semantic Layer" is the largest segment, accounting for 41.2% of the total, and is further subdivided into two primary categories: "Audio Difference Analysis" and "Aesthetic Analysis". The "Audio Difference Analysis" category includes subcategories such as "Signal Layer (4.3%)", "Anomaly Detection", "Acoustic Quality Analysis", and "Imagination". The "Aesthetic Analysis" category includes "Culture of Speaker", "Professional Knowl & Reasoning", and "Spatial Analysis". The "Perception" layer, which is the innermost and smallest segment, is composed of "Music Theory", "Counting & Statistics", "Environmental Perception & Reasoning", "Speaker Analysis", "Emotion & Intention", "Correlation Analysis", and "Temporal Analysis". The chart uses a color gradient from light to dark blue to differentiate between the layers and subcategories, with labels clearly indicating the name and percentage of each segment. The overall structure visually emphasizes the dominance of the Semantic Layer in the MMAR benchmark.
